title: Identity Systems
hook: If you still see yourself as someone who's bad at sales, you'll keep finding ways to avoid selling.
statement: You act like the person you believe you are.
explainer: Your actions follow your self-image. If who you say you are and what you actually believe don't line up, your habits default to the old version every time.
sop: Write one sentence on the identity you want, like 'I ship every day.'
Score your Identity clarity and Belief strength 1 to 10.
List 3 recent actions that went against that identity.
Fix one this week by acting like that person.
Repeat the aligned action daily until it's automatic.
equation_example: Identity 8, Belief 7. 8 × 7 = 56 out of 100. Higher means your actions will match who you say you are. Lower means there's a gap between what you claim and what you believe, so your actions drift elsewhere.
question: Write one sentence about who you want to be in business and one action that proves it.
closing_statement: Identity isn't declared once. It's proven by repetition.
caption:
Principle Nº 136: Identity Systems

If you still see yourself as someone who's bad at sales, you'll keep finding ways to avoid selling.

You act like the person you believe you are.
